The United India Insuarnce Company ... vs A.Nagesh And Anr on
20 June, 2023
 The Honourable Smt. Justice M.G.Priyadarsini
 Civil Miscellaneous Appeal No.70 Of 2009
Judgment:

entities.text: United India Insuarnce Company ... vs A.Nagesh And Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Aggrieved by the order dated 28.05.2008 in W.C.Case No.124 of 2004 passed by the learned Commissioner for Workmen's Compensation and Assistant Commissioner of Labour, Nalgonda, the opposite party No. 2/Insurance Company has filed the present appeal.
2. For the sake of convenience, hereinafter, the parties will be referred as per their array before the Commissioner.

3. The brief facts of the case are that the applicant has filed an application under the provisions of Workmen's Compensation Act, 1923 claiming compensation of Rs.3,00,000/- alleging that he was employed by the opposite party No.1 as driver on Auto bearing No. AP 9W 2944, which was insured with opposite party No.2.
On 27.11.2003 the applicant was proceeding on the said auto towards Uppal Bus Depot on the instruction of opposite party No.1.
When the applicant reached Uppal Tank Bund, another Auto came and dashed to the auto of the applicant from the front side, due to which the auto of the applicant fell down.
As a result, the applicant sustained grievous fracture injuries.
Thereafter, the 2 MGP,J CMA_70_2009 applicant was shifted to Gandhi Hospital, Secunderabad.
On 03.12.2003 the applicant took treatment in Sai Sanjeevini Hospital, Dilsukhnagar and discharged on 05.12.2003.
The applicant incurred Rs.25,000/- towards his treatment but he did not recover from the fracture injuries and thereby, he has become permanent disabled.
A case in Crime No.640/2003 of Uppal Police Station was registered under Section 338 of the Indian Penal Code against the driver of the auto, which was responsible for the accident.
The applicant is aged about 20 years as on the date of the accident and he was being paid Rs.3,000/- per month by the opposite party No.1.

Hence, the applicant has filed the application claiming compensation of Rs.3,00,000/-
against the opposite party Nos.1 and 2, who are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.

4. Inspite of notice, the opposite party No.1, failed to file his counter and thereby he was set ex-parte and whereas, opposite party No.2 filed counter denying the averments of the application including age, employment of the applicant under opposite party No.1, wages of the applicant, applicant having valid and effective driving license, the disability of the applicant assessed by the PW2 and finally prayed to dismiss the application.
On behalf of the applicant, PWs 1 and 2 were examined and Exs.A1 to A8 were marked.
Exs. A1
and A3

are the certified copies of FIR and charge sheet, Exs.A2, A4, A5 and A7 are the x-rays,
original discharge card issued by Sai Sanjeevini Hospital, Hyderabad, original case sheet issued by The United India Insuarnce Company ... vs A.Nagesh And Anr on 20 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/151602967/
1 Gandhi Hospital, Secunderabad and original disability certificate.

entities.text: United India Insuarnce Company ... vs A.Nagesh And Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Exs. A6
and A8 are the salary certificate and driving license of applicant.

On behalf of opposite parties, none was examined,
however, Ex.B1 copy of insurance policy was marked.

The Commissioner after considering the evidence on record, both oral and documentary, by determining the wages of applicant as Rs.2,934/- per month, loss of earning capacity as 40% and loss of disability as 60% and by applying the factor '224' for the age of injured being 20 years, has awarded compensation of Rs.1,57,731/-.
6. Aggrieved by the compensation awarded by the Commissioner, the opposite party No.2/insurance Company has filed the present appeal to set aside the impugned order.

7. Heard both sides and perused the record.
8.

The main contention of the learned counsel for the opposite party No.2 is that on the date of the accident, the 4 MGP,J CMA_70_2009 applicant was not having valid and affective driving licence as he is having only non-transport driving license.
The applicant was examined as AW1, who has reiterated the averments of the application in his chief examination.

As seen from the record,
learned counsel for the opposite party No.2 has not put a single suggestion with regard to applicant not possessing valid and affective driving license to drive the auto bearing No.AP 9W 2944 on the date of the accident.

It is specific case of the opposite party No.2 that the vehicle involved in the accident was passenger carrying commercial vehicle and driver should necessarily possess driving licence with the transport endorsement and badge.
However, the opposite party No.2 failed to adduce any evidence to that extent.
On the other hand, the applicant has filed Ex.A8 driving license.
It is not the case of the opposite party No.2 that the deceased was not holding any type of license at the time of the accident.

In United India Insurance Company Limited v. Annakutty and another1,
wherein it was held by Kerala High Court as under:
"3.

entities.text: United India Insurance Company Limited v. Annakutty and another1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is an admitted case that the deceased workman was an employee of the insured and that the accident occurred while he was driving the jeep and the accident resulted in his death.
It was on 28.3.2002.
When the accident has 2006 (1) SCT 225 5 MGP,J CMA_70_2009 resulted in the death of the workman, necessarily clause (b)(ii) of the proviso to Section 3(1) of the Act will have no application.

Wilful disobedience of an order or rule expressly framed for the purpose of securing such safety like the insistence of a driving licence will have bearing going by the said provision, only in respect of any injury not resulting in the death of the workman.
Necessarily even if there was any contravention of the provisions of law, the compensation shall have to be paid by the employer where ever death occurs as a result of the accident.
When there was a valid insurance policy, that liability shall be on the insurer.

Therefore absence of driving licence cannot be taken as a reason to deny the compensation, in cases like this where the accident resulted, admittedly in the death of the workman."
9.

In another authority in the Oriental Insurance Company Limited v. Jimmy2, the Kerala High Court held as under:

2 "3.

sentences.text: The employer and employee relationship cannot be disputed by the appellant.
The accident also is not disputed.
In such circumstances, whether the workman did have a proper licence or not, whether he is a Wireman, a Boiler Operator or Driver as the case may be, is not a matter for the concern of the insurer.
When the insurer had undertaken the liability that had 2004 ACJ 900 6 MGP,J CMA_70_2009 fallen upon the insured, necessarily the insurer has to discharge that burden.
If there is violation of the policy conditions, the insurer can seek appropriate remedy."

10. This Court in New India Assurance Company Limited v. Smt.N.Anjilamma and five others3 held as under:
"13.

entities.text: New India Assurance Company Limited v. Smt.N.Anjilamma and five others3
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: A perusal of the judgment in Swaran Singh's case (1 supra), it would disclose that the Hon'ble Apex Court held that the breach of policy condition e.g., disqualification of driver or invalid 2005 LawSuit (Ker) 280 driving licence of the driver, as contained in sub-section (2)(a)(ii) of section 149, have to be proved to have been committed by the insured for avoiding liability by the insurer.

Mere absence, fake or invalid driving licence or disqualification of the driver for driving at the relevant time, are not in themselves defences available to the insurer against either the insured or the third parties.

To avoid its liability towards insured, the insurer has to prove that the insured was guilty of negligence and failed to exercise reasonable care in the matter of fulfilling the condition of the policy regarding use of vehicles by duly licensed driver or one who was not disqualified to drive at the relevant time.
CMA No.4769 of 2004 decided on 27.10.2021 7 MGP,J CMA_70_2009

The insurance companies are, however, with a view to avoid their liability must not only establish the available defence(s) raised in the said proceedings but must also establish 'breach' on the part of the owner of the vehicle; the burden of proof wherefor would be on them.
The court cannot lay down any criteria as to how the said burden would be discharged, inasmuch as the same would depend upon the facts and circumstance of each case.

Even where the insurer is able to prove breach on the part of the insured concerning the policy condition regarding holding of a valid licence by the driver or his qualification to drive during the relevant period, the insurer would not be allowed to avoid its liability towards insured unless the said breach or breaches on the condition of driving licence is/are so fundamental as are found to have contributed to the cause of the accident.

The Tribunals in interpreting the policy conditions would apply "the rule of main purpose" and the concept of "fundamental breach"
to allow defences available to the insured under section 149(2) of the Act.

3 14.

entities.text: United India Insuarnce Company ... vs A.Nagesh And Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The contention of the learned counsel for the appellant that the said judgment is not applicable to the Workmen's Compensation Act is not considered valid.
Though it was given under 8 MGP,J CMA_70_2009 the Motor Vehicles Act, it is equally applicable to the Workmen's Compensation Act.
The Insurer could not avoid his liability towards the insured unless he proves that the breach was so fundamental to have contributed to the cause of the accident.
The deceased was not driving the vehicle at the time of the accident, but was crossing the road to attend the nature call by stopping his lorry.

As such, the policy conditions regarding driver not holding driving licence at the time of accident cannot be considered as fundamental breach that had contributed to the cause of the accident, so as to discharge the appellant from the liability.
The above judgment also discloses that the absence of the driving licence cannot be a reason to deny the compensation when there was a valid insurance policy.
As such, it is considered that the Commissioner had not committed any error in passing the award holding the Opposite Parties jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the applicants.
The order of the Commissioner was not contrary to law or probabilities of the case and was not liable to be set aside.
Hence, I do not find any merits in the appeal and therefore, the same is liable to be dismissed."
11. In the case on hand, as per Ex.B1, the insurance policy was in force as on the date of accident.

The policy conditions regarding driver not holding driving licence at the time of 9 MGP,J CMA_70_2009 accident cannot be considered as fundamental breach that had contributed to the cause of the accident to discharge the appellant from the liability.
It is not the case of the opposite party No.2 that the accident has occurred due to the contributory negligence on the part of the deceased.

In such circumstances, mere absence, fake or invalid driving license or disqualification of the driver for driving at the relevant time, are not in themselves defence available to the insurer against either the insured or the third parties.

12. The other contention of the learned counsel for the opposite party No.2 is that opposite party No.1, who is the owner of the insured vehicle did not appear before the Commissioner to admit the employer and employee relationship between the opposite party No.1 and applicant.
It is pertinent to note that in spite of service of notice, opposite party No.1 was set ex-parte.
The opposite party No.2 also failed to examine opposite party No.1.
However, the applicant has filed Ex.A6 Salary Certificate to show that he was working as driver under his employer i.e., opposite party No.1 with a monthly salary of Rs.3,000/-.

On considering the documentary evidence adduced by the applicant,
learned Commissioner has arrived to a conclusion that applicant was working as driver on the Auto 10 MGP,J CMA_70_2009 belonging to opposite party No.1 and he met with an accident during the course of his employment under opposite party No.1.
13.

In P. Narasimha Reddy and others v. K. Ramachander and another4, the High Court of Andhra Pradesh held as under;
"The 2nd respondent alone disputed not only the relationship of the employer and employee, but even the occurrence of accident.

Except having the luxury of putting some irrelevant and obnoxious questions in the cross- The United India Insuarnce Company ... vs A.Nagesh And Anr on 20 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/151602967/
4 examination to PW-1 and RW-1, the 2nd respondent has not chosen to lead any evidence to buttress its contention.

entities.text: United India Insuarnce Company ... vs A.Nagesh And Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In that view of the matter, the plea taken by the 2nd respondent, in its counter-affidavit, remained unproved, and without any basis.
Instead of ignoring the unproved version of the 2nd respondent, the Commissioner has taken it as a gospel truth and denied the entire benefit to the appellants under the Act.

By her acts and omissions in this regard, the Commissioner belied the hope of the Parliament that the rights of the workman and their dependants, under the Act,
would be better protected by entrusting the adjudication to the departmental authorities."

14. In North East Karnataka Road Transport Corporation v. Sujatha5 the Honourable Supreme Court held as under:
2004 (4) ALD 15 11 MGP,J CMA_70_2009 "9.

entities.text: North East Karnataka Road Transport Corporation v. Sujatha5
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
At the outset, we may take note of the fact, being a settled principle, that the question as to whether the employee met with an accident, whether the accident occurred during the course of employment,
whether it arose out of an employment, how and in what manner the accident occurred, who was negligent in causing the accident, whether there existed any relationship of employee and employer, what was the age and monthly salary of the employee, how many are the dependents of the deceased employee, the extent of disability caused to the employee due to injuries suffered in an accident, whether there was any insurance coverage obtained by the employer to cover the incident etc.
are some of the material issues which arise for the just decision of the Commissioner in a claim petition when an employee suffers any bodily injury or dies during the course of his employment and he/his LRs sue(s) his employer to claim compensation under the Act.

10. The aforementioned questions are essentially the questions of fact and therefore,
they are required to be proved with the aid of evidence.
Once they are proved either way, the findings recorded thereon are regarded as the findings of fact.

11. The appeal provided under Section 30 of the Act to the High Court against the order of the Commissioner lies only against the specific orders set out in clauses (a)
to (e) of Section 30 of the Act with a further rider contained in the first proviso to the section that the appeal must involve substantial questions of law.

12. In other words, the appeal provided under Section 30 of the Act to the High Court against the order of the Commissioner is not like a regular first appeal akin to Section 96 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 which can be heard both on facts and law.
The appellate jurisdiction (2019) 11 SCC 514 12 MGP,J CMA_70_2009 of the High Court to decide the appeal is confined only to examine the substantial questions of law arising in the case."

5 15.

entities.text: United India Insuarnce Company ... vs A.Nagesh And Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In view of the principle laid down in the above said authorities, it is clear that the above contention of the appellant - insurance company is not based on a question of law but it is purely a question of fact, which cannot be raised before this Court as per Section 30 of the Workmen's Compensation Act.

16. Learned counsel for the opposite party No.2 further contended that the injury sustained by the applicant is not mentioned in Schedule - I of the Act and moreover, though, the doctor assessed the physical disability at 20%, the learned Commissioner took loss of earning capacity at 40%.

It is pertinent to note that the applicant got examined PW2, who has examined the applicant at the time of the accident and he deposed that the applicant sustained fracture of dislocation of neck of humerus left and a disability of post traumatic stiffness of left shoulder.
He further deposed that the applicant cannot do his work as he did previously.

Though PW2 has assessed 20% disability, the learned Commissioner, after considering the injuries sustained by the applicant, age of the applicant, has rightly assessed the loss of earning capacity at 40%.

Under these circumstances, this Court is of the considered opinion that learned Deputy Commissioner, after considering all the aspects, has rightly come to the conclusion in awarding compensation to the applicant.

Thus, this Court is not inclined to interfere with the findings of the learned Commissioner and thereby the Civil Miscellaneous Appeal is liable to be dismissed.
18.
Accordingly, the Civil Miscellaneous Appeal is dismissed.
There shall be no order as to costs.

Pending Miscellaneous applications, if any, shall stand closed.
